sections.text: Introduction

This document covers the waste water treatment 
 plant of AL-Arish power station.

The sanitary plant will be under treatment by an 
 activated sludge plant, aeration basin, clarifier and Aerobic sludge 
 stabilization system, the plant operates continuously at a constant rate 
 therefore due to the high peaks in flow and concentration one equalization 
 basin has been provided with internal aeration in order to avoid bad smell 
 problems the plant has an extended aeration area with sludge 
 recirculation.

Time by time the sludge transfers to the storage 
 tank to digested before disposal the separated water from sludge will be 
 disposal directly to the proper disposal area or this separated water will be 
 flowed to the clarified water filter to be treated for reuse.The plant runs 
 on automatic mode and is controlled by PLC on the indoor also manual system is 
 provided to operate different equipments manually.

The first draft was initiated by chemist: Mohamed 
 Mahmoud Kaheel; reviewed by department director chemist: Bekheet Abd El-haleem 
 ;revised by quality control chemist: Saad Sadeeek Hassnen at EDEPC and 
 accepted by Eng. Mohamed El said Abd El ghfar; 
General Manager of Al-Arish 
 Power Station, and certified by eng. Ally Mostafa Al Lathy EDEPC inspection & 
 quality control head sector.
Information
General Activities

The system performs the following activities 
 during operation:

Sanitary waste water is collected in a tank after 
 preliminary comminutor process at the inlet of the screen pit.

Later this collected sanitary waste water is 
 lifted up by a pumping station and flowed to the aeration basin where an 
 activated sludge liquor provides an effective degradation of organic matter in 
 order to achieve an elevated oxygen transfer rate.

Fine air bubble diffusers are installed in order 
 to satisfy oxygen demand of activated sludge.

Liquor effluent from the aeration basin will be 
 flowed to the sedimentation tank where biomass will be separated from water as 
 sludge.

A certain amount of recovered sludge is recycled 
 back to the aeration basin in order to maintain an optimum value of sludge 
 concentration in the aeration basin.

A major amount of sludge is collected in 
 the sludge collecting tank where aeration diffusers assure the sludge to be 
 digested before disposal.

Sludge is usually accumulated and barried in 
 segregated sludge pits. To reuse this separated water, filters are provided 
 after filtration.
Basic Design

The system is designed on following 
 basis
Treatment Design

Screening Unit-Sewage or trade waste flow into the plant through 
 a screen. The function of the screen is to chop up solids such as rags without 
 removing them from the sewage flow.

Aeration Compartment- 
 The annular aeration compartments containing the 
 mixed liquor is fitted with coarse bubble air diffusers supported in clusters 
 on down pipes connected to the air header. In this compartment the build up of 
 microorganism is carried out and the weight of activated sludge gradually 
 increases. It is mentioned also that the microorganisms use the polluting 
 matter in the sewage as food and convert it to carbon dioxide, water and new 
 all material.

Settlement Compartment- The settlement tank is of the upward flow type 
 and is filled with an inlet stilling well, a mechanically driven sludge 
 scraper at the bottom and a mechanical surface skimmer. In this tank the 
 activated sludge will concentrate and settle to the bottom and sucked from the 
 bottom to the sludge storage tank.
Directives
Chemical Tests

There are some tests carried out during the 
 process of treatment to check and attain good work, these tests are:
PH

PH test must be carried out for the sanitary 
 water using PH meter in the chemical lab. For the correct functioning of the 
 biological processes, the PH value should be in the range 6.5- 8.5. Low PH 
 values encourage the growth of filamentous micro-organisms which hinder the 
 settlement of the activated sludge. Low PH values can be caused by the 
 discharge of acidic trade waste ( e.g. mineral acids or milk processing waste 
 water ) If the PH value is lower than the demand range, lime or soda ash can 
 be added.
Dissolved Oxygen

A good indication that the dissolved Oxygen 
 concentration is sufficient is given by superficial examination of the sludge 
 which should have only a faint earthy smell. A black or grey sludge having a 
 foul smell indicates that the air supply is insufficient. The Oxygen value is 
 measured also by Oxygen meter to determine the value.
Settlement Test

This simple test provides basic information 
 regarding the operation of the plant. A one liter measuring cylinder should be 
 filled with mixed liquor from the mixing aeration compartment and allowed to 
 stand for 30 min. The volume of sludge settled out should normally be in the 
 range 25-40 percent. If the volume is above 40 percent the mixed liquor solids 
 concentration should be checked. The supernatant liquor above the sludge layer 
 should be clear, free from excessive solids and should have a faint earthly 
 smell. A smell of hydrogen sulphide indicates that the air supply to the plant 
 is inadequate and should be increased. The sludge should be dark brown in 
 color. A grey or black color also indicates inadequate air supply.
Turbidity: By Spectrophotometer

The turbidity test measures an optical property 
 of the water sample which results from the scattering and absorbing of light 
 by the particulate matter present. The amount of turbidity registered is 
 dependent on such variables as the size, shape and refractive properties of 
 the particles.

In this method we zeroing by demineralized water 
 and determined the turbidity of the sample at 450 nm by ( NTU ) nephelomteric 
 turbidity unit.
Suspended Solids: By Spectrophotometer

This method of determining suspended solids is a 
 simple direct measurement which does not require the filtration or ignition 
 and weighing steps that gravimetric procedures do. The method measure the S.S 
 from ( O to 750 mg/L ).

We zeroing by deminerlaized water and blend the 
 sample by blender at high speed for exactly two minutes and remove gas bubbles 
 in the sample and measure the S.S of the sample
 at 810 nm.
Routine and Preventive Maintenance
Routine Check

The following check must be done before each 
 operation: The availability of raw water at inlet of the plant.
The functional status of each equipment.
The functional status of each instrument.

The working condition of sludge particles or 
 other dirt.

Before start up the plant the respective valves 
 opening and closing should be checked up.

Preventive 
Maintenance

Keep close the sluice gate in case of 
 unavailability of raw water to prevent against any sudden thrust of raw water 
 to the inlet equipments.

Sometimes air diffusers can be blocked up by fine 
 sludge particles or other dirt such as algae etc. which can be removed or 
 washed up by water from external source.

sections.text: Filling up Procedure for the Sand Filter

The filter should be filled up 
according to the following procedure

items:
Open the bottom manhole and hand 
 hole.

Insert through the bottom manhole 
 the largest size quartz grit (10/20 mm) careful.

Do the same operation with medium 
 size quartz grit (3/5 mm).

Close the manhole, pay attention 
 to the right position of gasket.

Pour through the top hand hole 
 the smallest size quartz grit (0.4/0.8 mm), 
 then 
 pour anthracite from the top through the same hand hole.
Now close the top hand hole.

After each five years of use 
 sands and anthracites should be substituted by fresh sands as because the 
 filtering capacity become weaken.

Before using sand filter a 
 backwashing should be executed in order to clean up inner dirts of filters.
